column1: # jespersen's own Irish word list (CC0): words respelt for what the spelling rules would miss.
# One per line: the word in lower case, a tab, its respelling. A ˈ marks a stress the rules
# Irish is read as Munster says it (decision 45), checked against M.-L. Sjoestedt's Phonétique
# d'un parler irlandais de Kerry (1931) and Description d'un parler irlandais de Kerry (1938),
# both public domain, used for their facts.
# Adverbs once compounded with a proclitic keep the stress on their second part (Phonétique,
# § 260: isteach, istigh, anois, inniu; Description, §§ 90–91: amuigh, amach, abhaile, anall,
# The forms of ag stressed on their second syllable (Description, § 107: acu əku, aige iˈgʹe,
# air erʹ (Description, § 108); is with a broad s (is maith, is é); raibh revʹ (Description,
# § 180). ag (eg, § 107) and ar (er, broad, § 108) are given in src/sentence.rs.
